projects.name: Tenstorrent stack
projects.summary: The open software stack for our Tenstorrent QuietBox 2. tt-metal (TT-NN ops + TT-Metalium kernels) is the core, tt-forge is the MLIR compiler for PyTorch/JAX, tt-inference-server serves models with vLLM, and tt-studio is a web GUI to deploy and chat with models. Latest tt-studio: v2.13.0 (Nov 2026), adding fine-tune job deletion, a guided fine-tune tour, ~6x faster Hugging Face Xet downloads and shared RAG collections. Latest tt-metal: v0.81.1 (Oct 23, 2026). Latest tt-inference-server: v0.26.0 (Oct 30, 2026) , adding QuietBox 2 support for K2-Horizon-7B, Muse-Glimmer-30B, Kolibri-1-BF16, gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and granite-4.2-30b.

projects.name: Flide
projects.summary: Inference server for decision/router models (Strands Decider, Perplexity's decider, Cloudflare's Clef and ~35 more families). Keeps agent state across steps so each step reads only what's new; claims up to 9.5x faster than vLLM and SGLang (unverified). CUDA/Triton only, so it won't run on QuietBox 2 as published.

projects.name: Strata
projects.summary: Local MoE inference engine (C++, built on llama.cpp's GGUF formats and ggml kernels) that runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE) on a consumer GPU with 12 GB or more. It keeps the hot experts in VRAM, the rest in system RAM computed on the CPU in parallel, and a lookup table on SSD. Also serves DeepSeek V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. One-click install for Windows/Linux, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API on localhost so Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode can use it, plus an MCP server. Supports NVIDIA RTX 30/40/50, AMD R9700 and Strix Halo, Apple Silicon (64 GB+); no Tenstorrent backend. Latest: v0.2.13 (Nov 9, 2026).

projects.name: Avalon
projects.summary: A llama.cpp fork built for one model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE), on one consumer AMD GPU. The dense weights, KV cache and the hottest experts stay in VRAM, the rest live in system RAM (or are read from NVMe when RAM is short), and the CPU computes the missed experts in parallel. Reports 98 tok/s on an RX 7900 XT with 64 GB DDR4 over PCIe 3.0, about 88 tok/s with 32 GB and about 49 tok/s with 16 GB, and fits 256k context in 20 GB VRAM. The installer is Linux plus ROCm only. Benchmarks itself against Strata; its GPU and CPU kernels were written by Claude Opus 5.5. No releases yet.

projects.name: QB2 agentic coding guide
projects.summary: Tenstorrent's Oct 27, 2026 step-by-step: serve Qwen3.8-27B on a TT-QuietBox 2 with tt serve , then connect OpenCode from a Mac with tt launch . One box batches up to 8 agents, and code never leaves your network.
projects.license: Guide (Apache-2.0 tooling) Caution DFlash2 drafter is CC BY-NC-ND (non-commercial)

projects.name: colibri
projects.summary: Pure-C, zero-dependency engine that runs frontier MoE models on your own hardware by streaming experts from disk.

projects.name: FreeToken
projects.summary: Runs 290B+ frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.6, GLM-5.2) on consumer RTX GPUs; OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API so Claude Code and Codex can run locally.

projects.name: Project Maya
projects.summary: Runs 321B–748B MoE models (GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) on your own 1–16 GPUs by tiering experts across VRAM, RAM and NVMe; OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API.
projects.license: MIT Caution Optional DFlash2 drafter is non-commercial (CC BY-NC-ND)

projects.name: AMD AI Playbooks
projects.summary: AMD's free step-by-step guides for local AI on Ryzen AI Halo, Ryzen AI Max+ and Radeon. They cover PyTorch on ROCm, LM Studio, Lemonade, Ollama, vLLM, ComfyUI, fine-tuning with Unsloth and LLaMA Factory, n8n with gpt-oss-120B, GAIA agents, and clustering two to four Halos over RPC or RCCL to run 350B+ models. Each guide has Windows and Linux steps, and AMD adds new ones every month.

projects.name: Lemonade
projects.summary: Open-source local AI server with an OpenAI-compatible API. It runs LLMs, image models and audio models on AMD GPUs and NPUs, and it's the default serving layer in AMD's Halo playbooks and Project Zenith.

projects.name: Strix Halo toolboxes
projects.summary: Community toolbox containers with llama.cpp built for Strix Halo, with Vulkan and ROCm backends. The quickest way to run llama.cpp on a 395 under Linux.

projects.name: GAIA
projects.summary: AMD's framework for building AI agents that run locally on Ryzen AI PCs. It has its own Halo playbook.

projects.name: TheRock
projects.summary: Lightweight open-source build system for HIP and ROCm. Use it to get current ROCm builds onto newer consumer chips like the Strix Halo iGPU.

projects.name: strix-halo-testing
projects.summary: Benchmarks and setup notes for Strix Halo running LLMs. Last updated October 2025, so the numbers predate newer ROCm releases.

projects.name: Gorgon Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495)
projects.summary: A refresh of Strix Halo on the same Zen 5 and RDNA 3.5 design, with 192GB LPDDR5X-8533 (up to 160GB usable as VRAM) and 273 GB/s of bandwidth, up from 256. AMD announced it May 20, 2026 and partner boxes shipped from Sep 28. Prices as of Nov 13, 2026: TOPC TXA2 $6,499, ACEMAGIC F9A $6,699 (pre-order), GMKtec EVO-X5 Pro $6,799 (in stock), Framework Desktop from $6,799 DIY, AMD Ryzen AI Halo $7,299.99 (Micro Center pickup only), Minisforum MS-S1 MAX-P495 $7,399 (sold out). It's only worth it over a 128GB box for models above about 120GB, such as Qwen3-235B or DeepSeek V4 Flash.

projects.name: Strix Halo 128GB boxes (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)
projects.summary: The value pick: 128GB at 256 GB/s for about half the price of a 192GB box. Prices as of Nov 12, 2026: Bosgame M5 $3,099 (pre-order), GMKtec EVO-X2 $3,499.99 (early Black Friday through Nov 22, with 30-day price match), Minisforum MS-S1 MAX $3,959. 128GB is the most the 395 supports, and the memory is soldered.

projects.name: Tenstorrent QuietBox 2 (Blackhole)
projects.summary: Your box: four Blackhole chips on two liquid-cooled p300c cards, with 128GB GDDR6 at 2,048 GB/s total (about 8x a Halo's bandwidth) and 720MB of SRAM. The host is a Ryzen 7 9700X with 256GB DDR5 and 4TB NVMe. It draws up to 1,300W and idles at 320W. Tenstorrent rates it for models up to 120B, and it ships with Qwen3-32B preloaded. Price as of Nov 13, 2026: $9,999, in stock, ships in 2 weeks plus 2 to 5 weeks transit. The original QuietBox (4x p150c, $11,999) and the Wormhole QuietBox ($15,000) are sold out. The p300c cards aren't sold separately.

projects.name: Tenstorrent Blackhole cards and Galaxy
projects.summary: The DIY route and the upgrade path. Blackhole p100a costs $999 (28GB, 448 GB/s, no links). The p150a (active) and p150b (passive) cost $1,399 each, with 32GB at 512 GB/s and 4x QSFP-DD 800G ports for pooling cards; the cable is $200, half off with two cards. Each card is 300W on PCIe 5.0 x16. The Wormhole n150 and n300 run $999 to $1,449. A February 2026 firmware update cut Blackhole to 120 Tensix cores (from 140), about a 1 to 2% hit by Tenstorrent's estimate. The Galaxy server is 32 chips with 1TB GDDR6 and 23 PFLOPS FP8 in 6U at 8 to 10 kW, listed at $160,000 (launched at $110,000 in April 2026). Tenstorrent raised a $1.5B Series E at a $6.2B valuation in Oct 2026.

projects.name: Clustering Halo boxes
projects.summary: AMD's playbooks cluster 2 to 4 Halos with llama.cpp RPC or RCCL to run 350B+ models, and 10GbE is enough for RPC's pipeline split. Tensor parallel needs RDMA, which USB4 can't do yet, so people add Mellanox or ConnectX NICs through a PCIe slot (MS-S1 MAX, wired x4; Framework Desktop, x4) or an M.2-to-OCuLink adapter. Networking by box: MS-S1 MAX and EVO-X5 Pro have 2x10GbE, TOPC TXA2 and AMD Halo 1x10GbE, Framework 5GbE, ACEMAGIC F9A 2x2.5GbE plus OCuLink.

projects.name: Siren Halo (formerly Medusa Halo)
projects.summary: The first real redesign after Strix Halo. Leakers say Medusa Halo (Zen 6, RDNA 5, LPDDR6) was renamed Siren Halo and adds dedicated GDDR7 VRAM next to LPDDR system memory. Gotou_3rd says there's no new Halo design in 2027, so likely 2028. AMD hasn't confirmed anything. Medusa Point (Zen 6 laptop chips) is expected in early 2027.

projects.name: Weight-Space Programming
projects.summary: Frontier LLMs reading and writing neural network weights directly, with no gradients and no training loop. GPT-6 Astra tells what a small network was trained on from its raw weights, and writes game-playing networks from scratch that beat PPO trained for 100M steps. Editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to fix a reasoning-loop fault raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and IFEval about 3x (same sampling settings). Blog post (Nov 2, 2026); logs and the edited model are public.
projects.license: Custom / unclear (logs repo) Caution Edited model is Apache-2.0

projects.name: nanochat
projects.summary: Minimal, hackable end-to-end LLM harness for one GPU node: tokenizer, pretraining, fine-tuning, RL, eval and chat. Trains a GPT-2-grade model in about 2 hours on 8×H100 for ~$48.

projects.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
projects.summary: Open weights for Moonshot's flagship: 2.8T-parameter MoE with 104B active and a 1M-token context. Far too large for a 128 GB QuietBox 2.

projects.name: DeepSeek
projects.summary: Frontier MoE models with open weights. Latest Flash is about 763B params with 1M context and native vision; V4-Pro-0813 is the flagship.

projects.name: Liquid AI LFM
projects.summary: Hybrid, on-device foundation models. LFM3 is six ~2B models for text, vision, audio, omni and decisions on one backbone. Also LFM2.5-24B-A2B (Oct 13, 2026): a 24B MoE with 2B active for on-device agents.
projects.license: LFM Open License v1.0 Caution Commercial use free only under $10M annual revenue

projects.name: GLM
projects.summary: Top open-weight coding models. GLM-5.3 is a 744B MoE with 40B active and 1M context. GLM-5.3-Flash (Aug 26, 2026) is a 320B MoE with 18B active plus vision, under MIT.
projects.license: GLM-5.3 License Caution Custom; Flash is MIT. Model-as-a-service providers over $10B revenue need Z.ai review

projects.name: OpenMausBot
projects.summary: Self-hosted open-source alternative to Grok Bot: an always-on agent with its own VM, trigger-driven runs, a Results chat that collects webhook and app-event reports, quote-grounded memory, and a Vault of 1Password secrets referenced by name. Trending, but established (v0.1.151, Nov 9).

projects.name: Strands Decider
projects.summary: Small, fast 'system one' model that picks between options or scores on a scale, with a confidence per decision: a router in front of worker models. Amazon's write-up claims it replaced Claude Sonnet 4.6 for ticket classification at ~44x lower cost and ~640 ms (unverified).

projects.name: DeepSeek Super-agent
projects.summary: One always-on agent across chat, GitHub and email. A filter screens events, a small, fast Router talks to people and hands out tasks, and isolated Workers each own one task, with the strongest model on the hard ones. Long jobs run async; a Watchdog catches stuck workers. In DeepSeek's simulation, p95 tasks finished in 15.7 min vs about 29 min for one session, at 2 to 4x the tokens.
projects.license: MIT Research prototype for DeepSeek Harness, not a product

projects.name: AgentBaton
projects.summary: Learns when to hand a long agent task from a capable model to a cheaper one, once. Cuts API cost 65.9% on average across 11 model pairs while largely keeping accuracy.
projects.license: CC BY 4.0 (paper) Caution Paper only, no code yet

projects.name: CAMEL
projects.summary: Multi-agent framework researching the scaling laws of agents.

projects.name: MetaGPT
projects.summary: Multi-agent "AI software company" turning natural language into software.

projects.name: Atomic Agents
projects.summary: Lightweight, modular building blocks for agents.

projects.name: GPTSwarm
projects.summary: Self-improving agent graphs via RL and prompt optimization.

projects.name: Burr
projects.summary: Build, trace, and persist decision-making apps and agents on your own infra.

projects.name: AREX-2
projects.summary: A 27B agent (Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune) trained to run the try, measure and revise loop itself instead of leaving it to the harness. It's trained on long ML-engineering and algorithm trajectories that keep their failed rounds. Scores 81.8 on MLE-bench Lite and 70.7 on Frontier-CS, and keeps improving over a 5-hour budget. Ablation: skills plus more rounds (harness) add 39 points, training adds 13.6. The repo holds eval runners only; the optimized harness isn't published.

projects.name: SWE-agent
projects.summary: Takes a GitHub issue and tries to fix it automatically (NeurIPS 2024).

projects.name: OpenHands
projects.summary: AI-driven software development platform.

projects.name: Agent Zero
projects.summary: General-purpose personal agent framework.

projects.name: Goose
projects.summary: A new memory-safe systems language from the creator of FlatBuffers and Lobster. It has no heap, no GC, no reference counting and no lifetime annotations: every value lives inline on compiler-managed data stacks, so freeing a million-element structure is a single store. Compiles a whole program to one C file and calls C directly; a bundled TinyCC backend runs programs in-process. Threads share no memory and pass flat values over typed queues. Claims 1.16x the speed of hand-optimized C++ and 1.12x safe Rust across 16 of its own benchmarks. Much of the code and docs are AI-written; 603 points on Hacker News (Nov 2026).

projects.name: billion-context
projects.summary: Context-compression proxy that keeps one agent session going for weeks: the model folds history into summaries and can unfold them later. Works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness; self-reports ~100K working context and 5x fewer tokens.

projects.name: auto-ontology
projects.summary: Python framework for semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data: deterministic query generation and better context retrieval for LLM agents.

projects.name: claude-mem
projects.summary: Persistent cross-session memory for coding agents: captures tool use, compresses it, and injects relevant context into later sessions (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Copilot).

projects.name: DSPy
projects.summary: Programming, not prompting, language models.

projects.name: Mem0
projects.summary: Drop-in persistent memory layer for agents.

projects.name: Letta
projects.summary: Stateful agents with long-term memory that self-improve.

projects.name: STORM
projects.summary: Researches a topic and writes a full cited report.

projects.name: H-Net
projects.summary: Tokenizer-free, byte-level architecture. A learned dynamic-chunking step replaces BPE tokenization inside the model, and stages can nest (bytes into words into phrases). Cartesia's Oct 28 posts claim a two-stage H-Net matches SmolLM3-3B with about 10x less compute and data; a Hugging Face Transformers PR adding it opened Oct 30.

projects.name: Buzz
projects.summary: Block's self-hosted workspace where humans and agents share rooms on a Nostr relay: agents are members with their own keys and audit trail, YAML workflows, approval gates, ACP harness for Goose/Codex/Claude Code. Buzz 1.0 moved to block/buzz-app.

projects.name: Plannotator
projects.summary: Human-in-the-loop workspace for coding agents: shape plans, annotate, review code and send all feedback back to the agent in one click.

projects.name: Trajectory
projects.summary: Observability for AI coding agents: captures sessions from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and about 20 more via hooks into local timelines, token and cost metrics, and YAML Markers (retries, force-pushes). Datadog LLM Observability export is optional and off by default.

projects.name: Unified Harness Protocol (UHP)
projects.summary: Open draft standard for driving complete agent harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini CLI) through one HTTP contract: tasks, streaming, sessions, files, cancellation. Shaped like the OpenAI Responses API, with a 104-check conformance suite. HarnessRouter is the self-hosted reference server.

projects.name: harness-eval
projects.summary: Did a harness change (AGENTS.md, skills, MCP, hooks) make a coding agent better or worse? Paired, repeated, isolated runs with per-task deltas, bootstrap CI, an A/A noise floor, and CI exit codes. Claude Code, Codex or Ollama.

projects.name: agent-desktop
projects.summary: Rust computer-use for agents via OS accessibility trees, with stable refs and retry-safe actions.

projects.name: OpenBot
projects.summary: Open-source AI coworkers, each with its own computer (browser, files, tools). Every action is approved before and logged after. Works with any AG-UI agent.

projects.name: Worktrunk
projects.summary: CLI that makes git worktrees as easy as branches, so you can run many coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) in parallel; adds hooks, LLM commit messages, one-command merge and shared build caches.

projects.name: Lightpanda
projects.summary: Headless browser built from scratch in Zig for AI agents; Puppeteer/Playwright via CDP, native MCP server, ~16x less memory than headless Chrome.

projects.name: Skyvern
projects.summary: AI browser workflow automation.

projects.name: AgentOps
projects.summary: Agent monitoring, LLM cost tracking, benchmarking.

projects.name: Composio
projects.summary: 1,000+ toolkits with auth and a sandbox so agents can take action.

projects.name: kagent 1.0
projects.summary: Kubernetes-native agent runtime (CNCF sandbox), now 1.0 (Nov 9, 2026) with Agent Substrate 1.0. Each agent is a sandboxed actor that suspends when idle and resumes on the next message from a snapshot. Adds human-in-the-loop approval pauses, scheduled runs, conversation checkpoints and forks, credentials injected at the egress gateway, and SPIFFE identity per agent. Runs Claude, Codex or a custom loop; needs Kubernetes 1.37+. Publisher of the sandbox series.

projects.name: Not All Agent Sandboxes Are Created Equally
projects.summary: Compares agent sandboxes on four axes: boundary and access controls, environment, lifecycle, and interface and experience. Advice: start with where the agent loop runs. First post in a series, with one follow-up per project.

projects.name: Google AX
projects.summary: Agent Executor: Google's open agentic orchestration runtime, which runs agent tasks on Agent Substrate.

projects.name: Agent Substrate
projects.summary: Kubernetes-based core for agent sandboxes. It suspends and wakes idle agents, and egress is denied by default.

projects.name: nono
projects.summary: Single binary that applies kernel-level restrictions to an agent, with an optional egress proxy.

projects.name: DefenseClaw
projects.summary: Security governance layer for agentic AI, built on NVIDIA OpenShell.

projects.name: Minimal
projects.summary: Runs an agent in a Minimal box: sandboxed sessions built from its own package registry, on your own computer.

projects.name: Discobox
projects.summary: Coding-agent sandboxes: a dev box per agent on a copy of the repo (discobox apply).

projects.name: Substrate env
projects.summary: Agentic environment abstraction: a shell, file and MCP API on Agent Substrate.

projects.name: Docker Sandboxes
projects.summary: A microVM per coding agent, each with its own Docker daemon.

projects.name: OpenShell
projects.summary: Policy-governed sandbox runtime for agent fleets. Declarative YAML policies enforced outside the agent: kernel-level file, syscall and network controls, egress proxy, credential brokering, and a formal policy prover. Runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Copilot CLI on Docker, Podman, microVM or Kubernetes.

projects.name: E2B
projects.summary: Secure cloud sandboxes for agents to run code.

projects.name: SPACE
projects.summary: Firecracker microVM sandbox behind Perplexity Computer: one VM per agent task, with credentials and network egress controlled outside the VM. E2B-compatible.
